---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(Synth)
```

A synthetic control estimate depends on the donor pool, matching predictors
and fitting periods. `synth_sensitivity()` refits `synth()` independently for a
declared set of designs, holding the treated unit, outcome, treatment date,
solver settings and ATT evaluation periods fixed.

Declare the designs before inspecting effects. These examples illustrate the
interface and do not establish that every design is equally credible.
Researchers must exclude known treated or contaminated donors and ensure that
precomputed predictor columns contain no future information. Calendar checks
cannot establish no anticipation, no spillovers or a stable untreated outcome
relationship after treatment.

```{r study}
data(smoking)
baseline <- list(
  outcome = "cigsale", unit_col = "state_id", time_col = "year",
  treated = 3, treatment_time = 1989,
  predictors = c("lnincome", "age15to24", "retprice", "beer"),
  pre_periods = 1980:1988,
  special_predictors = list(list("cigsale", c(1975, 1980, 1988), "mean"))
)
specifications <- list(
  baseline = list(),
  short_pre = list(pre_periods = 1984:1988),
  outcomes_only = list(predictors = NULL),
  invalid_window = list(pre_periods = 1980:1990)
)
res <- synth_sensitivity(smoking, baseline, specifications, att_periods = 1989:2000)
as.data.frame(res)
summary(res)
res$failures
```

`res$estimates`, also returned by `as.data.frame(res)`, has one row per design.
`summary(res)` describes dispersion across those estimates.
Each ATT is the mean observed-minus-synthetic gap over 1989--2000. `pre_rmse`
uses all observed pre-treatment periods for every specification; `fit_rmse`
uses its own fitting periods. The intentionally invalid design illustrates
failure retention. There is no automatic removal based on fit or effect size.
Warnings, including nonconvergence, are stored in `res$warnings`; finite
estimates from warning-bearing fits remain in the tables and plots.

```{r curve}
plot(res)
```

The curve shows every attempt. Failures have labels and no assigned effect
value; crosses identify fits with warnings. `summary(res)` reports attempted
and failed counts alongside the dispersion of finite estimates. Sign shares
describe the registered designs, not the probability of a causal effect.
The spread across designs is not a confidence interval.

```{r paths}
plot(res, type = "paths")
head(res$weights)
head(res$paths)
```

`res$registry` preserves each merged configuration; `res$baseline` preserves
the original baseline. `res$metadata` records the common periods, exclusions,
package version and resolved solver arguments. Native fits and preparation
objects remain in `res$fits` and `res$prepared`, including predictor weights
and optimizer output. Save the result with `saveRDS()` alongside the original
panel and the code declaring the registry.

For the older interface, use `interface = "dataprep"`, specify
`treatment_time` separately, and use `dataprep()` argument names. This permits
independent predictor-aggregation and outcome-fitting windows, plus arbitrary
special-predictor windows. Entries may be complete configurations with unchanged
study fields or just design overrides:

```{r advanced}
legacy <- list(
  dependent = "cigsale", unit.variable = "state_id", time.variable = "year",
  treatment.identifier = 3, controls.identifier = c(1, 2, 4, 5),
  predictors = "retprice", predictors.op = "mean",
  time.predictors.prior = 1980:1988, time.optimize.ssr = 1970:1988,
  special.predictors = list(list("cigsale", c(1975, 1980, 1988), "mean"))
)
advanced <- synth_sensitivity(
  smoking, legacy,
  list(late_fit = list(time.optimize.ssr = 1980:1988)),
  att_periods = 1989:2000, interface = "dataprep", treatment_time = 1989
)
as.data.frame(advanced)
```

This initial interface supports deterministic `ipop` fits. Pre-treatment
holdout validation and other solver backends need separate checks before being
added. Existing placebo inference remains a separate analysis: it changes the
putatively treated unit, while this registry changes its research design.
